plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: Spidery, ribbon-like petals unfurl on bare winter branches. They give off a sweet, spicy fragrance that carries across a frosty garden. The petals curl up in hard freezes and relax again when it warms.
plants.location: Temperate gardens of Europe and North America, native to central China
plants.funFact: Witch hazel seeds are shot out of their woody capsules with a pop. They can travel several meters from the parent shrub.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: Nodding white cup-shaped flowers with golden stamens rise from dark, leathery evergreen leaves. They often open through snow and are a cheerful sight in the depths of winter. As they age, the petals blush soft pink.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring, often peaking from December to February
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across Europe, native to the mountains of central and southern Europe
plants.funFact: What look like petals are really sepals. They stay on the plant for weeks, which is why the blooms last so long in the cold.

plants.name: Eucalyptus ficifolia
plants.description: In the southern summer, this tree is covered in dense, fluffy clusters of blossom. The blooms are made of masses of stamens, and they draw in nectar-feeding birds and bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern summer, roughly December to March
plants.location: Southwestern Western Australia, widely planted in Australian streets and gardens
plants.funFact: It has one of the smallest natural ranges of any eucalyptus, in a small patch of Western Australia. Even so, it is planted in warm regions around the world.
